findings.claim: Across the observed score window [0.0,0.49] the landmark_00_local_dx curve is non-monotone: it rises to a positive peak near t~0.10-0.11, falls to a negative trough near t~0.19, partially recovers near t~0.27, and ends slightly positive; the whole-window mean is near zero (whole_window_z=-0.18) with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches.

landmark_00_local_dy is predominantly negative over the window (whole_window_z=-0.30), with an early negative excursion near t~0.04-0.09, a brief positive segment near t~0.14-0.18, and a return toward zero at the end; 6 sign changes and 4 strong sign conflicts indicate batch-level disagreement.

landmark_00_local_dz shows a late-window negative drift: values are near zero early, become positive around t~0.28-0.40, then decline to a negative endpoint (last_z=-0.59, last_rate_z=-2.38), with 10 sign changes and 7 strong sign conflicts.

landmark_00_soft_mass is the most coherent of the read features: it rises from a slightly negative start to a sustained positive plateau near t~0.14-0.30 (peak values_z~1.6), then decays to a slightly negative endpoint; whole_window_z=+0.64 with only 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict.

landmark_01_local_dx and landmark_01_local_dy both show an early positive-to-negative swing (positive near t~0.02-0.08, negative trough near t~0.14-0.20) followed by partial recovery; landmark_01_local_dy is negative on average (whole_window_z=-0.50) while landmark_01_local_dx is near zero (whole_window_z=-0.22).

landmark_01_local_dz and landmark_01_soft_mass both rise from negative early values to positive mid-window values near t~0.14-0.20 and then relax toward zero; landmark_01_local_dz has whole_window_z=-0.01 and landmark_01_soft_mass whole_window_z=-0.25, both with 4-6 sign changes and 5-9 strong sign conflicts.

hypotheses.direction: encourage the observed positive mid-window soft-mass excursion relative to the near-zero early and late values
hypotheses.falsifier: If the soft-mass excursion is not reproducible across independent batches (strong_sign_conflicts rises above the observed 1) or if the mid-window plateau does not separate from the early/late baseline, the coordinate is not a stable control target.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass (predicted endpoint world-A soft mass at landmark 00)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate carries a coherent, batch-consistent positive mid-window excursion (rise from ~t=0.05 to a plateau near t=0.14-0.30, then decay), unlike the noisier dx/dy/dz components. A reward that tracks this soft-mass observable over the observed window would test whether the coherent mass signal, rather than the noisy per-axis displacement, is the useful control coordinate.

hypotheses.direction: encourage the observed positive-then-negative dx contrast pattern rather than a stationary target
hypotheses.falsifier: If the dx contrast is dominated by batch disagreement (9 strong sign conflicts observed) or the peak/trough positions are not stable across independent batches, the contrast is not a reliable control coordinate.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx (predicted endpoint world-A x-displacement at landmark 00)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate has a reproducible non-monotone shape (positive peak near t~0.10, negative trough near t~0.19, partial recovery near t~0.27) with a near-zero whole-window mean. A reward that tracks the sign of this contrast over the window would test whether the transient dx excursion, rather than its window average, is the informative control signal.

hypotheses.direction: encourage the observed late-window negative dz drift
hypotheses.falsifier: If the late-window dz decline is not reproducible across independent batches (7 strong sign conflicts observed) or the endpoint sign flips under resampling, the drift is not a stable control target.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dz (predicted endpoint world-A z-displacement at landmark 00)
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_local_dz coordinate drifts negative late in the window (positive near t~0.28-0.40, negative endpoint with last_rate_z=-2.38). A reward that tracks this late-window dz decline would test whether the terminal dz direction, rather than the early-window behavior, is the informative control signal.

limitations: Only landmark_00 and landmark_01 dx/dy/dz/soft_mass curves were read; the remaining 192 catalogue features (landmarks 02-19 and all local_cxx/cxy/cxz/cyy/cyz/czz components) were not observed and no hypotheses are offered for them.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available; all statements rest on the continuous curves only.

All read curves have polynomial_accepted=false and relative_node_RMSE between 0.29 and 0.78, so the fitted polynomial coefficients are not reliable summaries; only the observed node values and their z-scores were used.

Several features show 4-10 sign changes and 4-10 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so batch-level reproducibility is weak for the dx/dy/dz components; the soft_mass feature is the most coherent but still has 1 strong sign conflict.
These are selection-window coordinate contrasts, not measured guidance effects; no reward, dose, or affinity outcome is claimed here.

The clock observation confirms the learning window is [0.0,0.5] with recorded affinities removed and an equal score prior, so no decoded-affinity evidence is available to relate these coordinate contrasts to final affinity.
